text: Which interfaces or classes are in a database-specific JAR file? (Choose all that apply.)

correct.description: The Driver, Connection, Statement, and ResultSet interfaces are part of the JDK, making choices A and E incorrect. The concrete DriverManager class is also part of the JDK, making choices C and D incorrect. Choices B and F are correct since the implementation of these interfaces is part of the database-specific driver JAR file.

text: Which are required parts of a JDBC URL? (Choose all that apply.)

correct.description: A JDBC URL has three parts. The first part is the string jdbc, making choice C correct. The second part is the vendor/product name. The third part is database specific, but it includes a database name, making choice B correct as well. The location, such as IP address and port, is optional.

text: Which of the following is a valid JDBC URL?

correct.description: A JDBC URL has three main parts separated by single colons, making choices B, C, E, and F incorrect. The first part is always jdbc. Therefore, the correct answer is A. Notice that you can get this right even if you’ve never heard of the Sybase database before.

text: What file is required inside a JDBC 4.0+ driver JAR?

correct.description: Starting with JDBC 4.0, driver implementations were required to provide the name of the class implementing Driver in a file named java.sql.Driver in the directory METAINF/service.

text: Which of the following is the correct way to close a Connection, Statement, and ResultSet? (Choose all that apply.)

answers.text: Closing only the Connection will close the other two.
Closing only the Statement will close the other two.
Closing only the ResultSet will close the other two.
Using a try-with-resources statement will close them in the correct order.

correct.description: Choices B and C are correct. Connection and Statement both have a close() method. Choices A and D are incorrect because ResultSet and DriverManager do not have a close() method that would be used in this context (DriverManager is a utility class, and while ResultSet has a close() method, closing the Statement automatically closes its ResultSet).
